gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 16-inch 16:10 side screen is exactly as tall as a 17.3-inch 16:9 laptop panel (both 8.48 in), while a 15.6-inch 16:9 side screen is 0.83 in shorter and a 14-inch 16:9 one is 1.62 in shorter.
standout_why: I compared against WorkCocoon's 'Best 17-Inch Laptop Screen Extenders' (rank 1 in both chats) and Cevaton's '[2026] Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 17 Inch Laptops' (a rank-9 result). Neither gives a panel height, an aspect ratio or a PPI figure, and neither says whether the side screens line up with a 17-inch laptop's own panel. WorkCocoon only says in words that the same pixel count on a smaller panel gives higher density. Graded Picks could not be read because of a TLS certificate error, so it is not counted.
decides: This backs a 16-inch 16:10 extender as the size match for a 17.3-inch 16:9 laptop: the picture heights are the same, so the side screens' top and bottom edges line up with the laptop's. Of the screens we link, the FOPO S788 is one, and FOPO's own range (in our record) runs to 18.5 in. The FOPO S10 is the sourced dual fit (FOPO: '12.0–17.3-inch laptops'), but its 15.6-inch 16:9 panels are 0.83 in shorter than the laptop's. The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro and Duex Float 2 Pro list 15–16 in as their fit range in our records, so on the question's terms they fall out. If the 17-inch laptop is 16:10 (9.01 in tall), no 16-inch 16:10 side screen matches its height. The S11's fit range could only be seen in search snippets, so it stays out until the maker's page is read.
